newsitem.title: CHINA: China to establish listed firm survey system.
newsitem.headline: China to establish listed firm survey system.

text.p: China will tighten supervision of listed firms by creating a system under which several will be fully investigated each year to ensure their operations comply with the rules, the Shanghai Securities News said on Monday.
The newspaper published a circular from the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC), saying local officials, lawyers and accountants must all participate in the company checks.
The investigations will cover a wide range of items including the information release procedures of the listed firms, it said.
A CSRC spokesman was quoted by the newspaper as saying that the move was aimed at improving the quality of listed firms.
"The quality of listed firms is the foundation of the healthy development of China's securities markets," he said.
"Listed firms must fully cooperate with investigators," the rules said. "Those that are found violating rules will be punished."

The CSRC spokesman said that an experimental investigation into a number of selected listed firms in April to July last year had found many problems, prompting the securities authorities to promulgate the new rules.

"Some firms were found to have reported false profits, while others had misused share issue proceeds," he said. "Some were found to have violated rules in stock trading and others failed to release information on important company developments."
He said some lawyers and accountants had also collaborated with listed firms in the irregularities, he added.
